source.title: Types for tame p-adic groups
source.version: arXiv:1810.04198v2, 3 November 2020, 39 pages. Independently read all pages, including proofs and references; PDF SHA-256 unchanged from the extraction. Source findings are checked against rendered v2 pages. The Annals version was not read. On 23 September 2026 no correction was found on the arXiv version listing, journal landing page or author publication page.
readSections: Abstract and §1 Introduction, pp. 1–6: the statements of both main theorems, the theory of types after Bushnell–Kutzko, the comparison with Kim's approach, and the history for GL_n, SL_n, classical groups and inner forms
§2 Assumption on the residue field characteristic, pp. 7–8: Assumption 2.1 and Lemma 2.2 with its five consequences
§3 Almost strongly stable and generic elements, pp. 8–14: Definitions 3.1, 3.3, 3.5, Lemmas 3.2, 3.4, 3.6, 3.11, Corollaries 3.7, 3.8, Remarks 3.9, 3.10 and Proposition 3.12
§4 The datum, pp. 14–17: Definitions 4.1, 4.2, 4.5, 4.6, Remark 4.3 and Lemma 4.4
§5 Some results used to exhibit data, pp. 17–21: Lemma 5.1 and Corollaries 5.2, 5.3, 5.4
§6 Every irreducible representation contains a datum, pp. 21–25: Theorem 6.1 with Lemmas 6.1.1, 6.1.2, 6.1.3 and Remark 6.2
§7 From a datum to types, pp. 25–35: Lemmas 7.1, 7.3, 7.5, 7.6, 7.7, 7.8, 7.10, Corollaries 7.2, 7.4, 7.9, Theorem 7.12 and Remarks 7.11, 7.13
§8 Exhaustion of supercuspidal representations, pp. 35–37: Theorem 8.1, Remark 8.2 and Corollary 8.3
References, pp. 37–39, read in full to identify the inputs listed under prerequisites

summary: Independent review corrected and expanded the original 33 bundled items to 108 items (0 library, 9 planned, 99 missing), with each missing item routed once. Under tame splitting and residue characteristic prime to the absolute Weyl-group order, the paper constructs a contained datum for every irreducible smooth complex representation, extracts a Kim–Yu type after verifying all datum conditions, and proves exhaustion of supercuspidals by Yu compact induction. The field may have positive characteristic; tori are separate. Four routes distinguish general types/data/exhaustion, existing local-structure layers, the finite Weil extension of the metaplectic owner, and the good-characteristic/coadjoint extension of the upstream reductive-group owner. Existing SR category/Bernstein theory, mixed-characteristic GL_m type/segment theory, finite GL₂ character theory, group/root carriers and tame field arithmetic are imported. Five directly checked notational corrections in v2 are recorded, without a claim about the unread journal version. This is an extraction and routing review, not a completed proof blueprint or Lean build.

items.name: Bernstein decomposition
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. The smooth complex representation category is the product of blocks indexed by inertial classes of pairs (L,σ), with L a parabolic Levi and σ irreducible supercuspidal.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: An s-type
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For an inertial class s, a compact open K⊂G(k) and an irreducible smooth complex K-representation ρ form an s-type when every irreducible smooth π belongs to block s exactly when π restricted to K contains ρ.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: The type Hecke equivalence
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For an s-type (K,ρ), the Bernstein block R^s(G) is equivalent to unital left modules over the algebra of compactly supported ρ-spherical functions. Use the chosen dual/convolution convention when realizing this equivalence.
items.note: SR.1 supplies the ambient locally unital Hecke equivalence, not this type-specific unital block equivalence.

items.name: Standing tame and Weyl-order hypotheses
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. Fix a nontrivial additive character ϕ:k→C× of conductor the maximal ideal P, normalize val on k and extend that valuation to splitting fields without renormalizing. Sections 2–8 treat non-tori; the torus case consists of smooth characters and is handled separately.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), §1 conventions, pp.6–7; §2 and Assumption 2.1, p.7
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Tameness of the tori
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. Every k-torus in G splits over a tame extension.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), §2 after Assumption 2.1, p.7, citing [Fin19, Theorem 2.4 and Corollary 2.6]
items.note: Only the sufficient assertion is required. Optimality of the main bound is an expectation, not a necessity theorem about all representations.

items.name: Weyl-order restriction for Levi subgroups
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For every Levi subgroup of a parabolic of G over an algebraic closure, p does not divide its Weyl-group order.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: The bond-order bound
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. The prime p is larger than every bond order of the absolute Dynkin diagram, where bond order is the square of the ratio of the two root lengths.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: No bad prime for the coroot system
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For every closed subsystem Ψ of the coroot system Φ∨, ZΦ∨/ZΨ has no p-torsion.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: No torsion prime for either root system
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For every closed root subsystem Φ₀ of Φ, ZΦ∨/Z(Φ₀∨) has no p-torsion. The analogous assertion holds with Φ and Φ∨ interchanged.
items.note: Closure in Φ and closure in Φ∨ are different conditions; this item is distinct from /3c.

items.name: Prime-to-p indices of connection
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. The index [weight lattice:root lattice] of every root subsystem generated by a subset of a base of Φ is prime to p.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Every irreducible contains a Kim–Yu type
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. Every irreducible smooth complex representation of G(k) contains an s-type constructed by Kim and Yu.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Yu exhausts supercuspidals
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. Every irreducible smooth supercuspidal complex representation of G(k) arises from Yu’s compact-induction construction.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Theorem 8.1 and proof, p.36
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Supercuspidality criterion from a maximal datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). For any maximal datum (x,(X_i),ρ₀) contained in an irreducible smooth complex π, set G_{n+1}=Cent_G(ΣX_i). Then π is supercuspidal if and only if the facet containing x has minimal dimension in B(G_{n+1},k) and Z(G_{n+1})/Z(G) is anisotropic.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Moy–Prasad group filtration
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For x in the enlarged building and r≥0 define G_{x,r}, with G_{x,0} the connected parahoric, and G_{x,r+}=⋃_{s>r}G_{x,s}; deeper groups are normal in the shallower groups. The group filtration is not asserted at negative r.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Lie and dual Moy–Prasad lattices
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For every real r define g_{x,r} and g*_{x,r}, with the dual lattice characterized by X(g_{x,(-r)+})⊂P. Its elements also satisfy X(g_{x,-r})⊂O. Set g_r=⋃_x g_{x,r} and similarly for the dual. For an extension E with the extended k-normalized valuation, the tame comparison is (g_E)_{x,r}∩g=g_{x,r}.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), §3, p.8, equation (1), citing [Adl98, Proposition 1.4.1]
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Depth of a smooth representation
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For a nonzero smooth representation π, its depth is the least r≥0 for which V_π^{G_{x,r+}}≠0 at some building point x.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Depth of a coadjoint element
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For nonzero X in g_E*, d_E(x,X) is the largest r with X∈(g_E)*_{x,r}; put d_E(x,0)=∞ and d_E(X)=sup_x d_E(x,X). Omit E when E=k.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Graded Lie spaces and the reductive-quotient action
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. G_x is the connected reductive quotient of the special fibre of the connected parahoric at x; its residue-field points are G_{x,0}/G_{x,0+}, compatibly with unramified extensions. It acts on V_{x,r}=g_{x,r}/g_{x,r+}. A dual element of depth r reduces to V_{x,-r}* via the chosen lattice pairing.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Twisted Levi subgroups
items.statement: A smooth closed subgroup H′ of a reductive group H over F is a twisted Levi if it becomes a Levi of a parabolic after a finite field extension.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Images of twisted-Levi buildings
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For a twisted Levi G′⊂G, all relevant tori are tame. The embeddings over a tame splitting extension descend to B(G′,k)→B(G,k); the image is independent of the translation ambiguity of the embedding. It is the image, not a unique map, that is fixed.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Adler–Roche invariant lattice-compatible form
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. There is a nondegenerate G-equivariant symmetric k-bilinear form B on g whose isomorphism g→g* carries g_{x,r} onto g*_{x,r} for every x and r and whose restriction to every twisted-Levi Lie algebra is nondegenerate. Use B to embed (g′)* in g*.
items.note: Keep the full Weyl-order hypothesis and Lemma 2.2; prime-to-index-of-connection alone was an unsupported weakening in the original item.

items.name: Almost stable and almost strongly stable
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. A coadjoint element is almost stable if its geometric G-orbit is closed. It is almost strongly stable at x if it is almost stable and its depth reduction in V_{x,-d(x,X)}* is semistable for G_x, meaning that the geometric orbit closure does not contain zero.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: An almost strongly stable nonzero element attains its depth
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. If 0≠X∈g* is almost strongly stable at x, then d(x,X)=d(X).
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Centralizers of almost stable coadjoint elements
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. If X∈g* is almost stable, Cent_G(X) is a twisted Levi subgroup.
items.note: The proof uses the invariant form and good-characteristic root/centralizer arguments, not a general characteristic-zero assertion transferred without hypotheses.

items.name: Generic coadjoint elements
items.statement: An element X ∈ 𝔤* is generic of depth r at x ∈ B(G, k) if X is almost stable and there are a tamely ramified E/k and a split maximal torus T ⊂ Cent_G(X) ×_k E with x ∈ 𝒜(T, E) ∩ B(G, k), X ∈ 𝔤*_{x,r}, and for every α ∈ Φ(G, T) either X(H_α) = 0 or val(X(H_α)) = r, where H_α = dα̌(1); and if X(H_α) = 0 for all α then d(x, X) = r.
items.note: All standing hypotheses of /2 apply. Preserve the final central-case depth condition; it is essential.

items.name: Rootwise consequences of genericity
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. If X is generic of depth r at x and T is any split maximal torus in Cent_G(X) after extension, X(H_α)=0 on centralizer roots, val(X(H_α))=r on the complementary roots.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Generic nonzero elements attain their depth
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. If X≠0 is generic of depth r at x, then d(x,X)=d(X)=r.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Generic nonzero elements are almost strongly stable
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. If X≠0 is generic at x, then X is almost strongly stable at x.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Corollary 3.8 and proof, p.11
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Depth drops away from the centralizer building
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. Let X be generic of depth r at x and G′=Cent_G(X). For X′∈(g′)*_{r+} (the union of the deeper lattices over B(G′,k)) and y∈B(G,k) outside B(G′,k), d(y,X+X′)<d(X).
items.note: This is an inequality off a building, not the original extraction’s unspecified coset decomposition. Fintzen extends the proof of [KM03, Lemma 2.3.3] using /9 under the present hypotheses.

items.name: Generic perturbation with a nearby building point
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. Let r∈R and X be almost strongly stable at x with r=d(x,X). For every ε>0 there are x′ with d(x,x′)<ε and X̃∈X+g*_{x′,r+} such that X∈g*_{x′,r}, X̃ is generic of depth r at x′, and both x and x′ lie in B(Cent_G(X̃),k).
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Proposition 3.12 and proof, pp.12–14
items.note: No positive-depth restriction and no conjugacy assertion. The point may move; a deeper additive perturbation is required.

items.name: Extended data
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). An extended datum of G of length n is a tuple (x, (r_i), (X_i), (G_i), (ρ₀, V_{ρ₀})) with r₁ > ⋯ > r_n > 0 real, X_i ∈ 𝔤*_{x,−r_i} \ 𝔤*_{x,(−r_i)+}, twisted Levi subgroups G = G₁ ⊇ G₂ ⊋ ⋯ ⊋ G_{n+1}, x ∈ B(G_{n+1}, k), and (ρ₀, V_{ρ₀}) an irreducible representation of (G^der_{n+1})_{x,0}/(G^der_{n+1})_{x,0+}, subject to X_i ∈ 𝔤*_i, X_i generic of depth −r_i at x as an element of 𝔤*_i, and G_{i+1} = Cent_{G_i}(X_i). Allow n=0; then only x, G and an irreducible representation of the depth-zero derived quotient remain.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Data and truncated data
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). A datum is (x,(X_i),ρ₀), with ρ₀ an irreducible representation of (Cent_G(ΣX_i)^der(k)∩G_{x,0})/(Cent_G(ΣX_i)^der(k)∩G_{x,0+}), admitting an extended datum as in /14. A truncated datum omits ρ₀. The depths and centralizers determine the extension uniquely. The depth-zero ρ₀ need not be cuspidal.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Definition 4.2 and Remark 4.3, pp.15–16
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Moving the point of a truncated datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). If (x,(X_i)) is a truncated datum, then (y,(X_i)) is a truncated datum for every y∈B(G_{n+1},k), with the same depths and twisted-Levi tower.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Derived groups and mixed-depth filtration
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). For a truncated datum set H₁=G₁ if G₁=G₂, otherwise H₁=G₁^der, and H_i=G_i^der for i>1; put r_{n+1}=0. Define (H_i)_{x,s}=H_i(k)∩G_{x,s}. For extended real indices s≥t>0 with s/2≤t, (G_i)_{x,s,t} is the intersection with G(k) of the subgroup generated over a tame splitting field by T_s, roots in G_{i+1} at depth s and complementary roots in G_i at depth t. Put (H_i)_{x,s,t}=H_i(k)∩(G_i)_{x,s,t}; define the Lie lattices analogously. These groups are independent of the torus and splitting field.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: A representation contains a datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). With a datum as in /14a, π contains it if a subspace V′ of the vectors fixed by all (H_i)_{x,r_i+}, 1≤i≤n+1, realizes ρ₀ under (H_{n+1})_{x,0}, and each (H_i)_{x,r_i,r_i/2+}/(H_i)_{x,r_i+} acts on V′ by ϕ∘X_i under its Lie-quotient identification.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: A representation contains a truncated datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). π contains (x,(X_i)) if the vectors fixed by every (H_i)_{x,r_i+}, 1≤i≤n, contain a one-dimensional subspace on which each mixed-depth quotient at (r_i,r_i/2+) acts by ϕ∘X_i.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Maximal datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). A contained datum is maximal when the dimension of its point’s facet in the building of its terminal centralizer is at least the corresponding facet dimension for every other datum contained in π. This is facet-dimension maximality, not maximal sequence length.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: The commutator linear map and its lattice shift
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For r>0 and nonzero X generic of depth −r at x, choose a tame split maximal torus of G′=Cent_G(X). Let r″ be the k-subspace of complementary root spaces and j* the annihilator of g′ in g*. Then Y↦(Z↦X([Y,Z])) is an isomorphism r″→j* taking r″∩g_{x,s} onto j*∩g*_{x,s-r} for every real s.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Conjugating away a deeper coadjoint error
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. With /16, let r/2≤d<r and 0<ε<(r−d)/2. For C∈j*∩g*_{x,-(d+ε)} there is g∈G_{x,r-d-ε} such that Ad*(g)(X+C) agrees with X on g_{x,r} and vanishes on r″∩g_{x,d+}.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: The representation compatibility of the correction
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. With /16a, suppose V′ is fixed by G(k)∩⟨T(E)_{r+},U_α(E)_{x,(d+ε)+},U_β(E)_{x,r+}⟩, where α runs over roots outside G′ and β over roots in G′. If H⊂G′^der(k)∩G_{x,(2d-r+2ε)+} stabilizes V′, then g⁻¹Hg preserves V′ and its conjugate action is the original H-action on V′.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Mock exponential and its first-order adjoint estimate
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. At positive depth s the mock exponential used in Lemma 5.1 maps g_{x,s} to G_{x,s}; in chosen root coordinates it agrees with the ordered root-group product modulo G(E)_{x,2s}. Its adjoint action has linear term [Y,Z] modulo g_{x,t+2s} for Z∈g_{x,t}. This is a positive-depth approximation, not a convergent characteristic-zero exponential assumed in equal characteristic.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Correcting the j-th character
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). Let a truncated datum have length n>0, 1≤j≤n, r_j/2≤d<r_j and 0<ε<(r_j−d)/2. Choose T_j in Cent_{H_j}(X_j) as in Corollary 5.2. items.name: The missing D2 condition can be achieved
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. items.name: Yu’s supercuspidal construction with its input conditions
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). Start with tame twisted-Levi data satisfying Yu’s hypotheses: the terminal center modulo Z(G) is anisotropic, the depth-zero representation has irreducible supercuspidal compact induction to the terminal group, the point has maximal parahoric there, and the ordered depths and characters satisfy the prescribed genericity conditions. The construction forms a representation of the open compact-mod-center subgroup K̃=(G_{n+1})_[x](G_n)_{x,r_n/2}⋯(G_1)_{x,r_1/2}; its compact induction to G(k) is irreducible supercuspidal. items.name: The cover and Frobenius-reciprocity exhaustion argument
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). For supercuspidal π the Kim–Yu cover property forces M₁=G, hence M_{n+1}=G_{n+1} and Z(G_{n+1})/Z(G) anisotropic. Replace the enlarged-point stabilizer with the reduced-point stabilizer and construct ρ̃; compact induction of its depth-zero restriction to G_{n+1}(k) is irreducible supercuspidal by MP96 Proposition 6.6. Yu then gives an irreducible supercuspidal compact induction to G(k), and its nonzero Frobenius-reciprocity map to π is an isomorphism.

items.name: Kim–Yu types and G-covers
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). Under all Kim–Yu datum conditions D1–D5, including the generic embedding condition D2, the modified Yu construction produces a type which is a G-cover of a type for M₁=Cent_G(Z_s(M_{n+1})). The cover theorem supplies the supercuspidal-support restriction used in /25a.

items.name: Finite Stone–von Neumann theorem
items.statement: Let p be odd and H a finite Heisenberg p-group with center of order p and nondegenerate alternating commutator pairing on H/Z(H). For a fixed nontrivial complex character of Z(H), there is a unique irreducible complex H-representation with that central character, up to isomorphism.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), §7, pp.30–31, the Heisenberg-theory input to Lemma 7.8
items.note: The trivial central character does not have this uniqueness property. MP.1 treats locally compact characteristic-zero fields, not this finite theorem.

items.name: Finite Weil–Heisenberg representation
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional symplectic F_p-space V, p odd, and a nontrivial character of F_p, form H(V)=V×F_p with (v,a)(w,b)=(v+w,a+b+⟨v,w⟩/2). Choose the special isomorphisms and construct the genuine finite Weil extension to Sp(V)⋉H(V) used by Yu. A projective symplectic action alone does not supply this extension.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), §7, pp.30,32–33, citing [Yu01, Theorem 11.5] and [Gér77]
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Finite Weil restriction to a parabolic with its quadratic factor
items.statement: For the finite Weil–Heisenberg representation in /27a, let V=V⁺⊕V⁰⊕V⁻ be a polarized decomposition with V⁰ nondegenerate, and P the stabilizer of V⁺. The V⁺-invariant subspace contains the representation of P obtained from its maps to GL(V⁺) and Sp(V⁰) by tensoring the quadratic determinant character on GL(V⁺) with the Weil representation of V⁰. The quadratic factor must be retained.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Lemma 7.10 proof, p.33, citing [Gér77, Lemma 2.3(c), Theorem 2.4(b)] and footnote 3
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Unipotent fixed vectors used in the cuspidality proof
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). In Lemma 7.10, for the image of the finite unipotent radical U_f in P_i⊂Sp(V_i), the quadratic character on GL(V_i⁺) is trivial, and a further parabolic restriction on V_i⁰ produces a line fixed by that image. Hence each oscillator factor has a nonzero subspace fixed by U_f and by the positive-root isotropic subgroup U_i,f; their tensor product is used with a noncuspidal constituent of ρ to contradict maximality.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: The smooth complex representation category
items.statement: For a locally profinite group, a complex representation is smooth when every vector has open stabilizer; use its abelian category and subrepresentation/invariant-subspace operations.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: The ambient Hecke algebra and smooth modules
items.statement: For the locally pro-p group G(k) with complex coefficients, compactly supported locally constant convolution functions form a locally unital Hecke algebra and smooth representations correspond to its nondegenerate modules.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), §1, p.3, background to the type Hecke algebra
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Compact induction and its reciprocity
items.statement: For an open subgroup J of a locally profinite group and a smooth complex J-representation τ, compact induction consists of equivariant locally constant functions supported compactly modulo J; Hom_G(c-Ind_J^G τ,π)≅Hom_J(τ,π|_J).
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Admissibility and supercuspidal support
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. Use admissibility of irreducible smooth complex representations and supercuspidal support with its inertial equivalence class.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), §1, pp.2–4 and Theorem 8.1 proof
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Enlarged buildings and connected parahorics
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. Use B(G,k) with apartments, facets, the group action, reduced/enlarged comparison, connected parahoric models and their reductive special-fibre quotients. A full point stabilizer is distinguished from the connected parahoric.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), §1 conventions, pp.6–8 and §3, pp.8–11
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Absolute root data and their subgroup structure
items.statement: For a reductive group and maximal torus use its absolute roots, coroots, Weyl group, root lattices, bases, parabolics and Levi subgroups, with the standard root-combinatorial identities.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), §1 conventions, pp.6–7; Lemma 2.2, pp.7–8
items.note: This planned item excludes bad/torsion-prime definitions and index-of-connection arithmetic, now separately missing in /30a–c and /3–3e.

items.name: Bad primes for a root system
items.statement: For a finite reduced crystallographic root system Ψ, p is not bad in the convention used here when ZΨ/ZΨ₀ has no p-torsion for every closed subsystem Ψ₀⊂Ψ. In Lemma 2.2(c) take Ψ=Φ∨.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Torsion primes for a root system
items.statement: For a finite reduced crystallographic root system Φ, p is not a torsion prime in the convention used here when ZΦ∨/Z(Φ₀∨) has no p-torsion for every closed subsystem Φ₀⊂Φ.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Lemma 2.2(d), p.8, after [Ste75, Definition 1.3]
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: The index of connection
items.statement: The index of connection of a finite root system is the finite index of its root lattice in its weight lattice. Use the same definition on root subsystems generated by subsets of a base.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Tame local-field extensions
items.statement: For a nonarchimedean local field k with residue characteristic p, a finite extension is tame when its ramification index is prime to p (the residue fields are perfect). Use the tame absolute-Galois quotient with its wild-inertia kernel.
items.note: This field-theoretic item excludes tame descent of buildings, which is /8a.

items.name: Geometric semistability and closed orbits
items.statement: For a rational representation of a reductive group over a field, a vector is semistable in the affine convention used here when the closure of its geometric orbit avoids zero. A closed geometric orbit is the separate condition used for almost stability.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Definition 3.1, p.9; Corollary 3.8 proof, p.11
items.note: LP3’s good filtrations and invariant cohomology do not assert this orbit theory.

items.name: Rational destabilizing cocharacters over a perfect field
items.statement: Let a reductive group over a perfect field act rationally on a finite-dimensional vector space. If a rational vector is unstable, there is a cocharacter defined over that field whose limit on the vector at zero is zero. This is used over the finite residue field.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Corollary 3.8 proof, p.11; Lemma 6.1.2 proof, p.24, citing [Kem78, Corollary 4.3]
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Lifting destabilizing cocharacters and moving building points
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For a residue-field cocharacter in the parahoric reductive quotient, choose a split torus in the parahoric lifting a maximal split torus containing its image, lift the cocharacter, and choose a tame maximal torus of the generic fibre containing it. Its apartment contains x; small shifts x+ελ give the root-filtration inequalities used in §§3,6,7.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Corollary 3.8 proof, p.11; Lemma 6.1.2 proof, p.24; Lemma 7.10 proof, p.32
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Cuspidality for a finite reductive quotient
items.statement: For a connected reductive group Q over a finite field f, an irreducible complex representation of Q(f) is cuspidal if its invariants under U(f) vanish for the unipotent radical U of every proper f-parabolic. Apply this to the connected reductive quotients of parahorics.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Lemma 7.10 and proof, p.32
items.note: Finite GL₂ character theory is an existing special case; Clifford theory does not supply this general parabolic predicate. No Deligne–Lusztig classification is needed here.

items.name: Unrefined minimal K-types
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. At depth zero an unrefined minimal K-type is a cuspidal irreducible representation of G_{x,0}/G_{x,0+}; at positive depth it is a nondegenerate character of G_{x,r}/G_{x,r+}, where nondegeneracy means the corresponding dual coset has no unstable element (equivalently no nilpotent element after the invariant-form identification).
items.note: Introductory background; the proof uses the finer contained data rather than assuming these minimal types already determine a Bernstein block.

items.name: Existence of maximal data
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). Every irreducible smooth complex π has a maximal contained datum: Theorem 6.1 gives a contained datum and the integral facet dimensions are bounded, so one can maximize the dimension. This is independent of the subsequent minimization of the genericity defect.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Opening of §7, p.25; Theorem 7.12 proof, p.34
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: A datum alone need not determine a Bernstein component
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). A maximal datum can occur in different Bernstein components. Enhancing the datum to the relevant representation of (M_{n+1})_x determines the Bernstein component, using KY17 Theorem 10.3 with the HM08 hypothesis removed by Kal19 Corollary 3.5.5.
items.note: Do not confuse a bare datum with an s-type; this prevents a false classification claim.

items.name: Smooth character extension for the torus quotients
items.statement: For the locally compact abelian torus-quotient groups used on pp.26–27, a smooth complex character on the indicated open positive-depth subgroup extends to the whole group. The restriction agrees with the given character and the extension remains smooth since its kernel contains the original open kernel.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), §7 character construction, pp.26–27, Pontryagin-duality input
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Parabolics and unipotent radicals from cocharacters
items.statement: For a connected reductive group over the finite residue field, use an f-defined cocharacter λ with the unipotent radical of a given f-parabolic characterized by lim_{t→0}λ(t)gλ(t)⁻¹=1. Its lift supplies the apartment direction in Lemma 7.10.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Lemma 7.10 proof, p.32, citing [CGP15, Corollary 2.2.5 and Proposition 2.2.9]
items.note: The upstream structure-theory layer explicitly includes the dynamic cocharacter approach to parabolics/Levis/unipotent radicals; the parahoric lift is a separate /32b obligation.

items.name: A nonoptimal-depth coset has unstable reduction
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. If a coadjoint element has d(x,X)<d(X), the deeper-lattice coset at x is degenerate (contains an unstable element); its image in the corresponding dual graded space is unstable. Use the Adler–DeBacker result with the non-simply-connected qualification recorded at the start of their §3 and the Moy–Prasad graded-coset comparison.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Lemma 3.2 proof, p.9; Proposition 3.12 proof, p.14, citing [AD02, Corollary 3.2.6] and [MP94, Proposition 4.3]
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Almost stable representatives of filtration cosets
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For a building point y and real r, every coset modulo g*_{y,r+} has an almost stable representative; via the invariant form choose a semisimple representative. This supplies the representatives used to define f in the recursion.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Closed orbits of semisimple Lie elements
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. Under the invariant form g≃g*, an element in the Lie algebra of a maximal torus is semisimple and has closed geometric adjoint orbit; the corresponding coadjoint orbit is closed. This proves almost stability of the generic perturbation.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Proposition 3.12 proof, p.14, citing [Bor91, §9.2]
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: A generic element annihilates root spaces
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For X generic and any split maximal torus of Cent_G(X) after extension, X vanishes on every root subspace of g over that extension.
items.locator: arXiv:1810.04198v2 (3 November 2020), Lemma 3.6, final assertion, p.10
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Continuity on the finite locus
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). For f in /19 the subset f⁻¹(R≥0) is open in B_j and f is continuous on it, by comparing nearby root filtrations and applying simultaneous correction.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: The finite locus is closed and is the whole building
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). For f in /19 its finite locus is closed; since it is nonempty and open and B_j is connected, f is finite everywhere.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

items.name: Attainment of the recursive minimum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of arbitrary characteristic with residue characteristic p, and G a connected reductive k-group split over a tame extension, with p not dividing its absolute Weyl-group order. For the non-torus construction assume G is not a torus (hence p is odd). The G_j(k)-invariant continuous nonnegative function f in /19 attains a minimum on B_j, using a bounded fundamental domain. Choose x_j minimizing f and r_j=f(x_j)≤f(x_{j−1})≤r_{j−1}.
items.note: Independently checked against the cited public-preprint passage; see the review report for the owner and library search.

prerequisites.citation: Jiu-Kang Yu, Construction of tame supercuspidal representations, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 14 (2001), 579–622
prerequisites.why: The general tame twisted-Levi construction and its Heisenberg special isomorphisms, full genericity conditions, irreducibility and restriction theorems. Current ET.6 already owns mixed-characteristic GL_m type/segment theory, which is a special case to import and compare.

prerequisites.citation: Ju-Lee Kim and Jiu-Kang Yu, Construction of tame types, in Representation Theory, Number Theory, and Invariant Theory, Progr. Math. 323 (2017), 337–357
prerequisites.why: The general tame twisted-Levi construction and its Heisenberg special isomorphisms, full genericity conditions, irreducibility and restriction theorems. Current ET.6 already owns mixed-characteristic GL_m type/segment theory, which is a special case to import and compare.

prerequisites.citation: Colin J. Bushnell and Philip C. Kutzko, Smooth representations of reductive p-adic groups: structure theory via types, Proc. London Math. Soc. 77 (1998), 582–634
prerequisites.why: General reductive-group s-types, the unital type-Hecke block equivalence and G-covers. Import the already planned Bernstein decomposition SR.3 and the ET.6 mixed-characteristic GL_m case.

prerequisites.citation: Allen Moy and Gopal Prasad, Unrefined minimal K-types for p-adic groups, Invent. Math. 116 (1994), 393–408, and Jacquet functors and unrefined minimal K-types, Comment. Math. Helv. 71 (1996), 98–121
prerequisites.why: The filtration subgroups G_{x,r} and lattices 𝔤_{x,r} and the notion of the depth of a representation, in which the entire paper is written; the atlas plans parahorics and congruence subgroups but not this filtration.

prerequisites.citation: Ju-Lee Kim, Supercuspidal representations: an exhaustion theorem, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 20 (2007), 273–320
prerequisites.why: The previous exhaustion theorem, in characteristic zero and for very large p, by matching summands of the Plancherel formula. Remark 7.11 records that its Proposition 17.2(2) is false as stated, so this paper's Lemma 7.10 cannot cite it.

prerequisites.citation: Jeffrey D. Adler and Alan Roche, An intertwining result for p-adic groups, Canad. J. Math. 52 (2000), 449–467
prerequisites.why: AR00 Proposition 4.1 gives the invariant lattice-compatible form used in Remarks 3.10 and Lemmas 3.4/3.11. Corollary 3.2.6 belongs to Adler–DeBacker (AD02), not this paper.

prerequisites.citation: Ju-Lee Kim and Fiona Murnaghan, Character expansions and unrefined minimal K-types, Amer. J. Math. 125 (2003), 1199–1234
prerequisites.why: Lemma 2.3.3 is the off-centralizer-building depth inequality. Fintzen Lemma 3.11 explains why its proof works under the present weaker characteristic hypotheses.

prerequisites.citation: Tasho Kaletha, Regular supercuspidal representations, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 32 (2019), 1071–1170
prerequisites.why: The exactness of the depth filtration on a short exact sequence of tori that are tame over k, quoted as Lemma 7.1 and used to compare the filtration subgroups of a twisted Levi with those of its derived group.

prerequisites.citation: Jessica Fintzen, Tame tori in p-adic groups and good semisimple elements, Int. Math. Res. Not. 2021 (2021), 14882–14904
prerequisites.why: Theorem 2.4 and Corollary 2.6 there show that Assumption 2.1 forces all tori of G to be tame, and that outside a short list of types the assumption is also necessary — the evidence that the bound on p is optimal.

prerequisites.citation: Mark Reeder and Jiu-Kang Yu, Epipelagic representations and invariant theory, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 27 (2014), 437–477
prerequisites.why: The general tame twisted-Levi construction and its Heisenberg special isomorphisms, full genericity conditions, irreducibility and restriction theorems. Current ET.6 already owns mixed-characteristic GL_m type/segment theory, which is a special case to import and compare.

prerequisites.citation: Colin J. Bushnell and Philip C. Kutzko, The Admissible Dual of GL(N) via Compact Open Subgroups, Ann. of Math. Stud. 129, Princeton, 1993
prerequisites.why: The model case: the construction of all supercuspidal representations of GL_n(k) and the existence of types for every irreducible representation, which underlies the explicit local Langlands correspondence for GL_n and which the general theorems here reproduce.

prerequisites.citation: Tonny A. Springer and Robert Steinberg, Conjugacy classes, in Seminar on Algebraic Groups and Related Finite Groups, Lecture Notes in Math. 131 (1970); Robert Steinberg, Torsion in reductive groups, Adv. Math. 15 (1975), 63–92
prerequisites.why: The definitions of bad and torsion primes used in Lemma 2.2(c) and (d); the atlas plans root data but names neither notion.

prerequisites.why: Finite Weil–Heisenberg representations and parabolic restriction. Fintzen p.33 footnote 3 explicitly restores the quadratic factor missing from the printed statement of Gérardin Theorem 2.4(b). The present review checks Fintzen’s use, not a new independent audit of Gérardin.

prerequisites.citation: Jeffrey D. Adler and Stephen DeBacker, Some applications of Bruhat–Tits theory to harmonic analysis on the Lie algebra of a reductive p-adic group, Michigan Math. J. 50 (2002), 263–286
prerequisites.why: Corollary 3.2.6 and the beginning-of-§3 qualification are used in Fintzen Lemma 3.2 and Proposition 3.12. This corrects the misattribution to Adler–Roche.

prerequisites.citation: Jeffrey D. Adler, Refined anisotropic K-types and supercuspidal representations, Pacific J. Math. 185 (1998), 1–32
prerequisites.why: Tame lattice base change (1.4.1), mock exponentials (§1.5) and the adjoint approximation (1.6.3), used in §3 and Lemma 5.1.

prerequisites.citation: George R. Kempf, Instability in invariant theory, Ann. of Math. 108 (1978), 299–316
prerequisites.why: Corollary 4.3 supplies a rational destabilizing cocharacter over the perfect residue field. Current LP3 good-filtration theory is not a substitute for this missing theorem.

prerequisites.why: The enhanced-datum equivalence used through KY17 Theorem 10.3 in Remark 6.2; retain the removal of the additional hypothesis by Kal19 Corollary 3.5.5.

prerequisites.why: Fintzen cites VI.1 Proposition 24 for extending the rationally closed subsystem to a base, VI.2 Proposition 7 for the index dividing the Weyl order, and VI.4.5–VI.4.13 for Weyl orders. Reuse existing root carriers; the missing prime/denominator consequences remain to prove.

prerequisites.why: Fintzen cites §9.2 for closed semisimple orbits and §14.25 in the coadjoint-centralizer argument. The general upstream group structure is already an import; the specific orbit/centralizer comparison is additional. Bibliographic locators are recorded from Fintzen, not claimed as a full reread of the book.

routes.title: Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: types, depth and the construction of supercuspidal representations
routes.brief:
Begin with Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) as the first prerequisite. Import its early smooth abelian category SR.0:abelian-category, ambient Hecke algebra SR.1, compact induction and reciprocity SR.2, and complex admissibility, supercuspidal support and Bernstein decomposition SR.3. Do not depend on the late integral SR.6 or rebuild these objects. The targets, for k any nonarchimedean local field, G connected reductive split over a tame extension and p prime to the absolute Weyl-group order, are Fintzen Theorem 7.12 (every irreducible smooth complex representation contains a Kim–Yu s-type), Theorem 8.1 (every irreducible smooth supercuspidal is a Yu compact induction), and Corollary 8.3 (for a maximal contained datum, supercuspidality is equivalent to minimal facet dimension in the terminal-centralizer building and anisotropy of its center modulo Z(G)). Separate tori; the non-torus construction has p odd. Do not claim necessity or optimality of the bound, an algorithm classifying all representations, or that a bare datum determines a block.

Build general s-types, their unital type-Hecke block equivalence and G-covers. Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6) already owns the mixed-characteristic GL_m supercuspidal/type and segment theory: import that special case and compare the general theory to it; construct no second GL_m classification, segment theory or local Langlands correspondence. The general tame-group/equal-characteristic extension here remains necessary. The finite-reductive cuspidality predicate needed at depth zero is a parabolic-invariant predicate on the existing finite-representation carrier; compare its GL₂ case to Tau Ceti CharacterTheory layer 9 and reuse its finite induction/restriction infrastructure. No Deligne–Lusztig classification is required.

Develop depth, almost strong stability and generic dual elements; prove the off-centralizer-building inequality and the nearby-point generic-perturbation theorem with its epsilon quantifier and deeper additive coset. Define extended, truncated and contained data including the exceptional H₁ convention, length zero and facet-dimension maximality. Prove all parts of Lemma 5.1 and Corollaries 5.2–5.4 with their depth bounds and preserved subgroup actions. Construct the recursive function f, prove its equivariance, finite open/closed locus, continuity, minimum and almost strongly stable minimizer, then extend truncated data until the strict centralizer chain terminates. Keep the Adler–DeBacker degeneracy comparison and mock-exponential inputs explicit.

Construct the depth-zero Levi and intermediate subgroup, extend the torus characters, and prove every part of Lemma 7.3, including full Yu genericity. Define all five K-products, extended characters and the common kernel; prove all four product identities and construct the individual and combined Heisenberg quotients on those actual groups. Import finite oscillator theory from the finite extension proposed in route 3; do not rebuild it here. Extract ρ⊗κ only on the chosen irreducible K-subrepresentation V̂. Prove its depth-zero constituents cuspidal using the corrected quadratic-factor finite Weil restriction and the maximal-facet contradiction. Then minimize the genericity defect among maximal data and prove D2; D1,D3,D4,D5 alone produce a representation, not the final type. Use the cover property, reduced-building stabilizer, depth-zero compact induction to G_{n+1}(k), Yu irreducibility, and Frobenius reciprocity to prove exhaustion.

Import buildings, valued roots, parahorics and the local inputs in route 2 from Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1–3). Import rational orbit instability and good-characteristic root/centralizer facts from route 4, retaining its staged dependencies. Import tame ramification from Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification layers 3–4. Use the public v2 paper’s precise locators and corrected sourceIssues; its reported warnings about Kim07, KY17 D5 and Gérardin must accompany the dependency contracts. Formalizers must read those prerequisite papers before closing their leaves.
routes.reason: The existing SR.0–3 contracts provide ambient category theory and Bernstein blocks but no general tame-group data or exhaustion construction. The original route’s GL_m absence claim is stale: ET.6 already owns that special case. The revised route imports it and removes generic finite oscillator and reductive orbit theory into their own foundational extensions. The local structural input remains in RG2.1–3.

RG2.1 owns valued root-group filtrations and commutator estimates, RG2.2 buildings and their reduced/enlarged geometry, and RG2.3 connected parahorics, reductive quotients and congruence subgroups. Supply their blueprint with the exact real-indexed Moy–Prasad group/Lie/dual refinements, tame base-change and twisted-Levi building images, invariant form with lattice compatibility, mixed-depth groups and mock-exponential estimates, positive-depth exact sequences of tame tori, torus/derived generation and lifting of cocharacters. These are missing proofs within the existing local-structure layers, not a claim that those layers already prove them. Keep r≥0 for groups, r real for Lie lattices, r>0 for torus exactness, the valuation normalized on k, and the full Weyl-order hypothesis for the form. Import absolute root data from Tau Ceti and the new good-prime consequences from route 4. Representation depth, contained data, characters, types and exhaustion remain in route 1.

routes.title: Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels, Part II: finite Weil–Heisenberg representations
routes.brief:
Take Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms) as the parent and first prerequisite. Its current MP.0–2 scope begins with characteristic-zero local fields; it does not supply finite fields or the genuine finite symplectic action needed in Fintzen §7. Extend the shared Heisenberg/polarization definitions to finite symplectic spaces in odd characteristic, proving compatibility with the existing half-pairing algebraic construction rather than creating a second abstract central-extension carrier. This finite branch must use finite sums and algebraic complex representations; it must not wait for Haar integration, local metaplectic double covers or automorphic theta analysis. Import finite-group representation, induction, tensor and Schur/Clifford infrastructure from Tau Ceti RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction and the pinned libraries after checking exact hypotheses.

The endpoints are finite Stone–von Neumann uniqueness for a specified nontrivial central character, a genuine Weil–Heisenberg representation of Sp(V) semidirect H(V) after the prescribed special isomorphism and normalization, and Gérardin’s parabolic restriction with the quadratic determinant character retained. For V=V⁺⊕V⁰⊕V⁻, identify the V⁺-invariant model under the parabolic with the quadratic GL(V⁺) factor tensor the Weil representation of V⁰. Supply the iterated isotropic fixed-vector consequence consumed in Fintzen Lemma 7.10. Do not identify an arbitrary projective action with a linear Weil extension or import the local-field nonsplitting conclusion into the finite setting. Require p odd and the central character nontrivial; the trivial-character uniqueness claim is false. Source the precise theorem from Gérardin 1977, with Fintzen v2 p.33 footnote 3’s correction, and Yu 2001 §§10–11. The p-adic filtration groups, their special isomorphisms and the assembly of κ across a twisted-Levi tower remain in SmoothRepresentationsPartII; this extension exports only their reusable finite representation theory. Check a symplectic plane, zero-dimensional V, changes of polarization and the quadratic factor in a parabolic restriction.
routes.reason: An independent atlas-wide search finds the common oscillator owner MP.0–2, contrary to the original extraction’s claim of no Heisenberg/Weil owner. Its full README explicitly restricts its starting field to characteristic zero and requires a separately sourced extension for other characteristics. A finite Part II preserves that boundary and prevents a second oscillator theory hidden in the tame-types roadmap.

routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: good characteristic and coadjoint invariant theory
routes.brief:
Start with Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups) as the first prerequisite: its rational representations, Lie/adjoint objects, tori, parabolics, Levi subgroups and absolute root data are fixed suppliers, especially layers 1–7. Import root combinatorics from Tau Ceti RepresentationTheory/RootSystems. This extension owns only the missing root-prime arithmetic and orbit-theoretic statements required by Fintzen §§2–3 and §6. Do not rebuild group schemes, a reductive-group classification, or the dynamic construction of parabolics. Do not claim LanglandsParameterStacks:LP3 already supplies this theory: its integral good filtrations and invariant cohomology have a different contract.

First define bad primes, torsion primes and the index of connection with the distinct root/coroot closure conditions. Prove each part of Fintzen Lemma 2.2 separately under p prime to the absolute Weyl-group order: inheritance for geometric Levi subgroups, the bond-order bound, no bad prime for the coroot system, no torsion prime for either system, and prime-to-p indices for base-generated root subsystems. Keep the root-lattice/weight-lattice denominator and coroot differential consequences used in Proposition 3.12 explicit. Export these early results to ReductiveGroupsPartII’s invariant-form construction; this early branch must not depend on that form.

Define geometric orbit closure and affine semistability for rational representations. Prove the rational destabilizing-cocharacter theorem over a perfect field in Kempf Corollary 4.3’s setting, in particular over the finite residue fields in the paper. Separate this residue-field theorem from assertions over the possibly imperfect local field k. On the actual adjoint/coadjoint representation, prove the closed-orbit result for semisimple toral elements and Fintzen Lemma 3.4: under the tame/Weyl-order hypotheses an almost stable coadjoint element has a twisted-Levi centralizer. The latter branch may import the already-constructed Adler–Roche identification from ReductiveGroupsPartII and the upstream dynamic/semisimple centralizer theory; it must not feed back into the early good-prime proof. Prove root-subsystem and connected-centralizer identifications rather than assuming an arbitrary stabilizer is Levi. Export the orbit statements to SmoothRepresentationsPartII’s generic perturbation and recursive-depth arguments. Building points, parahoric cocharacter lifts and filtration inequalities stay with ReductiveGroupsPartII, and type/cuspidality constructions stay with SmoothRepresentationsPartII. Sources are Fintzen’s explicit proofs, Kempf 1978, Springer–Steinberg/Steinberg, Borel, and Bourbaki at the locators recorded in the extraction.
routes.reason: Full reads of the upstream reductive-groups document and LP3 show that the former owns carriers, tori, parabolics and root data and the latter good-filtration/cohomology statements. Neither plans rational orbit destabilization or the stated bad/torsion-prime arithmetic. These reusable missing foundations should extend the foundational reductive-group owner, not be declared supplied by LP3 or rebuilt inside a single smooth-representation construction.
